rules.title: Prohibition on Pre-Offer Criminal Record Inquiries in Housing Applications
rules.requirement: A housing provider must not require an applicant to complete any housing application containing criminal record inquiries prior to providing a conditional offer. The provider may only consider whether the applicant has been convicted of methamphetamine manufacture on federally assisted housing premises or is subject to lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.exemptions: Convictions for drug-related criminal activity involving the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on federally assisted housing premises, or being subject to a lifetime state sex offender registration requirement.; The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
A
housing provider
shall not require an applicant to
complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an
applicant’s criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer,
except that a housing provider may consider whether an applicant has ever been
convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production
of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether
the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State
sex offender registration program.

rules.title: Prohibition on Pre-Offer Oral or Written Inquiries
rules.requirement: A housing provider must not make any oral or written inquiry concerning an applicant's criminal record prior to extending a conditional offer.
rules.exemptions: The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
A housing
provider
shall not make any oral or written inquiry
regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.

rules.title: Applicant Right to Submit Mitigating Evidence or Inaccuracies
rules.requirement: An applicant is entitled to provide evidence to the housing provider showing inaccuracies in the applicant's criminal record, evidence of rehabilitation, or other mitigating factors.
rules.exemptions: The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
An applicant
may provide evidence to the housing
provider demonstrating inaccuracies within the applicant's criminal record or
evidence of rehabilitation or other mitigating factors.

rules.title: Mandatory Disclosures Prior to Accepting Application Fee
rules.requirement: Before accepting any application fee, a housing provider must provide written disclosure informing the applicant whether eligibility criteria include reviewing criminal history, along with a statement that the applicant may provide evidence of record inaccuracies, rehabilitation, or mitigating factors.
rules.exemptions: The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
Prior to
accepting any application fee, a housing provider shall disclose in writing to
the applicant:
(1)   Whether the eligibility criteria of the housing
provider include the review and consideration of criminal history; and
(2)   A statement that the applicant, pursuant to
subsection a. of this section, may provide evidence demonstrating inaccuracies
within the applicant's criminal record or evidence of rehabilitation or other
mitigating factors.

rules.title: Nondiscriminatory Application of Screening Standards
rules.requirement: A housing provider must apply the standards governing application procedures and inquiries to each applicant in a nondiscriminatory manner.
rules.exemptions: The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider
shall apply the standards established by this section to each applicant in a
nondiscriminatory manner.

rules.title: Prohibited Criminal Records in Applicant Evaluations
rules.requirement: A housing provider must not evaluate an applicant, before or after extending a conditional offer, based on arrests or charges not resulting in conviction, expunged convictions, executive pardons, vacated or nullified convictions, juvenile delinquency adjudications, or sealed records.
rules.exemptions: The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]

rules.title: Permissible Criminal Records After Conditional Offer
rules.requirement: Following a conditional offer, a housing provider may only consider convictions for specified severe crimes, lifetime sex offender registration offenses, or indictable offenses within defined lookback windows: 6 years for first-degree offenses, 4 years for second- or third-degree offenses, and 1 year for fourth-degree offenses.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies after issuance of a conditional offer to an applicant.
rules.exemptions: The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
After the issuance of a conditional offer to an
applicant, a housing provider may only consider a criminal record in the
applicant’s history that:
(1)   resulted in a conviction for murder, aggravated
sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, sexual assault in
violation of N.J.S.2C:14-2, causing or permitting a child to engage in a
prohibited sexual act or in the simulation of such an act in violation of
paragraph (3) of subsection b. of N.J.S.2C:24-4, or any crime that resulted in
lifetime registration in a state sex offender registry;
(2)   is for an indictable offense of the first degree
that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison sentence that
sentence concluded, within the six years immediately preceding the issuance of
the conditional offer;
(3)   is for an indictable offense of the second or
third degree that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison
sentence that sentence concluded, within the four years immediately preceding
the issuance of the conditional offer; or
(4)   is for an indictable offense of the fourth degree
that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison sentence that
sentence concluded, within one year immediately preceding the issuance of the
conditional offer.

rules.title: Standard for Withdrawal of Conditional Offer
rules.requirement: A housing provider may withdraw a conditional offer based on an applicant's criminal record only if the provider establishes by a preponderance of the evidence that withdrawal is necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest.
rules.exemptions: The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider may withdraw a
conditional offer based on an applicant's criminal record only if the housing
provider determines, by preponderance of the evidence, that the withdrawal is
necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest.

rules.title: Written Notice of Conditional Offer Withdrawal
rules.requirement: If a housing provider withdraws a conditional offer, the provider must furnish the applicant with written notification setting forth specific reasons for withdrawal and granting an opportunity to appeal by submitting evidence of inaccuracies, rehabilitation, or mitigating factors.
rules.exemptions: The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
If a housing provider withdraws a conditional
offer, the housing provider shall provide the applicant with written
notification that includes, with specificity, the reason or reasons for the
withdrawal of the conditional offer and an opportunity to appeal the denial by
providing evidence to the housing provider demonstrating inaccuracies within
the applicant's criminal record or evidence of rehabilitation or other
mitigating factors.

rules.title: Individualized Assessment Factors for Withdrawal
rules.requirement: The housing provider must conduct an individualized assessment considering the offense's nature and severity, the applicant's age at the time, time elapsed, rehabilitation and conduct evidence, potential impact on safety of tenants or property, and connection to rented or leased property.
rules.exemptions: The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
The housing provider shall perform an
individualized assessment of the application in light of the following factors:
(a)   the nature and severity of the criminal offense;
(b)   the age of the applicant at the time of the
occurrence of the criminal offense;
(c)   the time which has elapsed since the occurrence
of the criminal offense;
(d)   any information produced by the applicant, or
produced on the applicant's behalf, in regard to the applicant's rehabilitation
and good conduct since the occurrence of the criminal offense;
(e)   the degree to which the criminal offense, if it
reoccurred, would negatively impact the safety of the housing provider's other
tenants or property; and
(f)   whether the criminal offense occurred on or was
connected to property that was rented or leased by the applicant.

rules.title: Applicant Request for Relied-Upon Records
rules.requirement: An applicant may request, within 30 days of the withdrawal notice, a copy of all information relied upon by the housing provider, and the housing provider must provide the records free of charge within 10 days of receiving a timely request.
rules.exemptions: The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
(1)  The applicant may request, within 30 days
after the housing provider's notice of the withdrawal, that the housing
provider afford the applicant a copy of all information that the housing
provider relied upon in considering the applicant, including criminal records.
(2)   A housing provider shall provide the information
requested under paragraph (1) of this subsection, free of charge, within l0
days after receipt of a timely request.

rules.title: Prohibition on Discriminatory Housing Advertisements
rules.requirement: A housing provider must not knowingly or purposefully publish or cause to be published any advertisement explicitly stating that applicants with arrest or conviction records will not be considered, except regarding methamphetamine manufacture on federally assisted housing premises or lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.exemptions: Advertisements concerning convictions for methamphetamine production on federally assisted housing premises or lifetime sex offender registration.; The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider shall not knowingly or
purposefully publish, or cause to be published, any housing advertisement that
explicitly provides that the housing provider will not consider any applicant
who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses, except
for
drug-related criminal activity for the
manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally
assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime
registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program.

rules.title: Prohibition on Discriminatory Rental Statements and Applications
rules.requirement: A housing provider must not print, publish, circulate, display, post, mail, or use application forms or inquiries expressing unlawful limitations or discrimination regarding criminal records, except as permitted under the act or for methamphetamine production on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.exemptions: Exceptions permitted by this act, convictions for drug-related criminal activity involving manufacture of methamphetamine on federally assisted housing premises, or lifetime sex offender registration.; The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider
shall not print, publish, circulate, issue, display, post, or mail, or cause to
be printed, published, circulated, issued, displayed, posted or mailed any
statement, advertisement, publication or sign, or use any form of application
for the rental, lease, or sublease of any real property or part or portion
thereof or make any record or inquiry in connection with the prospective
rental, lease, or sublease of any real property or part or portion thereof
which expresses, directly or indirectly, any unlawful limitation, specification
or discrimination as to criminal record, except as permitted by this act and
for drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of
methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the
applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex
offender registration program.

rules.title: Restrictions on Dissemination and Use of Criminal Records
rules.requirement: Unless required by law, a housing provider must not distribute or disseminate an applicant's criminal record to unauthorized persons or use the record for any purpose inconsistent with the act.
rules.exemptions: Unless otherwise required by law.; The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
Unless otherwise
required by law, a housing provider shall not:
(1)   distribute or
disseminate an applicant’s criminal record to any person who is not expected to
use the criminal record for the purpose of evaluating the applicant in a manner
consistent with this act; or
(2)   use an applicant’s
criminal record for a purpose that is not consistent with this act
.

rules.title: Prohibition on Drug/Alcohol Testing and Treatment Facility Inquiries
rules.requirement: A housing provider must not require an applicant to undergo a drug or alcohol test, nor request an applicant's consent to obtain records or information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
rules.exemptions: The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider shall not require an applicant
to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to
obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.

rules.title: Interference and Retaliation Prohibited
rules.requirement: No person may interfere with, restrain, or deny the exercise of rights protected under the act, and unlawful retaliatory actions against a person for filing a complaint constitute separate and distinct violations.
rules.exemptions: The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
A person shall not interfere with, restrain, or
deny the exercise of, or the attempt to exercise, any right protected under
this act.  If the division determines that a housing provider has engaged in
one or more unlawful actions against a person with the intent of retaliating
for the person’s filing of an action against the housing provider pursuant to
section 12 of this act, then each unlawful retaliatory action shall be
enforced, pursuant to section 12 of this act, as a separate and distinct
violation of this act.

rules.title: Ground for Eviction Following Overturned Remedial Placement Order
rules.requirement: Notwithstanding the Anti-Eviction Act, if a court overturns a director's order placing an applicant into a rental unit, the finding that the housing provider did not violate the act constitutes grounds to evict the tenant upon providing at least 45 days' prior notice.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when a court overturns a director's order that compelled housing provision to an applicant who resides in the unit as a result of that order.
rules.exemptions: The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.interaction: Applies notwithstanding any contrary provision of the Anti-Eviction Act, P.L.1974, c.49 (C.2A:18-61.1 et seq.).
rules.quoted_span:
Notwithstanding any provision of the Anti-Eviction Act, P.L.1974, c.49
(C.2A:18-61.1 et seq.) to the contrary, if an appeal by a
housing provider is successful, and the court overturns a final decision of the
director that resulted in an order under this paragraph, then a determination
that the housing provider did not violate the provisions of this act as evidenced
by such successful appeal shall be grounds for the housing provider to evict
the former applicant if that person resides in a rental dwelling unit owned by
the housing provider as the result of the director’s order, so long as the
housing provider provides the applicant with at least 45 days’ notice prior to
the eviction;

rules.title: Remedy of Rental Application Fee Refund
rules.requirement: The director may order a housing provider who violated the act to return the applicant's rental application fee, unless housing is provided to the applicant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applicable upon a finding of violation unless housing is provided to the applicant.
rules.exemptions: The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
Unless housing is provided to the applicant
pursuant to paragraph (2) of this subsection, the director may require that the
applicant’s rental application fee be returned

rules.title: Applicant Compensation from Penalty Proceeds
rules.requirement: The director may require that a portion of the penalty owed by a violating housing provider, up to $1,000, be paid directly to the applicant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies upon a finding that a housing provider has violated a provision of the act and is assessed a penalty.
rules.exemptions: The act does not apply to dwelling units in owner-occupied premises containing not more than four dwelling units. [C.46:8-54; document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
The director may require that a portion of the
sum owed by the housing provider pursuant to subsection c. of this section be
paid to the applicant in an amount not to exceed $1,000.
